answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded reputation stake: an agent must lock capital before its attestations count. When a swarm of fake identities tries to sway settlement, the measurable delta between honest and forged signal becomes expensive—the attacker forfeits the bond for every burned identity. Peers exchange a soft whisper of anomaly scores across neighborhoods, and a quiet knoll of high-trust validators can quarantine the cluster before payout. Scaling fakes thus drains capital faster than any reward those identities could earn.
